# Endlink Bedrock block joining faces. Generated: do not edit by hand.
#
# One line per Bedrock block state that a fence, glass pane, iron or copper bar or wall reaches out
# to, and nothing for the ones none of them touch. The id is the hashed block network id a 1.26.40 to
# 1.26.45 backend sends; the word is sixteen bits, one per side and joining kind, laid out exactly as
# Java's own rule answers it: bit (side * 4 + kind) is set when a joining block of that kind standing
# on that side of this block reaches it. Sides are north, south, west, east in that order, and the
# kinds are 0 wooden fence, 1 glass pane and bar, 2 wall, 3 nether brick fence.
#
# Provenance. The facts are Java's, because 1.26.50's minecraft:connection_* states exist for parity
# with Java, and they were extracted by running the official Java server's own connectsTo and
# attachsTo against its own registry for every block state on every side - not by restating the rule.
# That extraction, and the Bedrock-to-Java block-state mapping used to key it by Bedrock id, are both
# Apache-2.0 generated artifacts of the viaendlink-next project:
#
#   viaendlink-next  java-protocol-latest/.../java-776-connections.txt   (tools/GenerateJava776Connections.java)
#   viaendlink-next  endlink-plugin/.../bedrock-2168-blocks.txt          (tools/GenerateBedrockBlockMapping.java)
#
# whose own inputs are Mojang's official Java server and block report, CloudburstMC/Data's Bedrock
# 2168 block palette (Apache-2.0) and GeyserMC/mappings (MIT). No GPL-licensed work is involved at
# any step, which the licence separation in WORKSPACE.md requires.
#
# Checked on generation against blocks whose answer is known from Java's source: stone, dirt and
# glass are reached on all four sides by every kind; barrier is reached by none, because Java's
# isExceptionForConnection excludes it; an oak fence is reached by fences and by nothing else; and a
# glass pane is reached by panes and walls but never by a fence.
bedrock 2169
kinds 4
